html:
1What You Will Learn

Note

Acronyms in this note. JSON: JavaScript Object Notation; API: application programming interface

  • Prompt engineering: clear instructions, few-shot examples, system versus user placement, output constraints, iterative refinement
  • Input sanitization and where instructions live across the prompt
  • Output handling: structured output, response validation, defensive parsing, and skepticism toward confident output

2Prompt Engineering

Running case

Tidewater's Vague Summaries

  • The prompt says: "Summarize the claim."
  • Adjusters get summaries of random length and detail, sometimes missing the loss date or the claimed amount
  • The team wants consistent, useful summaries
Principle What to do Claims example
Instruction clarity Be specific and direct: task, audience, length, what to include, what to omit "Write a 5-line summary for an adjuster: loss date, cause, claimed amount, coverage status, open questions"
Give context Explain the purpose and the audience "Adjusters decide within two minutes whether to escalate"
Examples (few-shot) Show 2 to 5 diverse examples of input and output, including edge cases One example with missing data showing "Not stated"
System versus user System: stable role, rules, format, tone. User turn: the task and the data for this request Rules in system; the claim text and question in user
Output constraints State the format, length, fields, and what to do when unsure "If a field is missing write Not stated; never guess"
Structure the prompt Use tags or headings to separate instructions, documents and questions <policy>…</policy>, <claim>…</claim>
Think before answering For hard tasks let the model reason (adaptive thinking or ask for step-by-step reasoning in a separate field) Coverage analysis
Iterate Change one thing at a time, run the evals, keep what improves the score Compare prompt v3 with v4 on the test set

  • Placement across components: put stable instructions in the system prompt, per-request data and the task in the user message, and tool descriptions in the tool definitions. Repeating a critical rule at the end of a long prompt can help.
  • Prompt adjustment is empirical: if the model skips a rule, make it more specific, add an example, or move it; do not just add capital letters.
  • Input sanitization: treat user-supplied text as data. Strip or escape characters that could break your tag structure, limit length, and never let user text change the system rules (Module 13).
Exam tip

Inconsistent or vague output almost always means the prompt is vague: add specific criteria, a format and examples before reaching for a bigger model.

3Output Handling

Technique What it does
Structured output Ask for JSON that matches a schema: use structured outputs (output_config.format with a JSON schema) or a tool with an input schema (strict mode); this removes syntax errors
Response validation After parsing, validate types, required fields, ranges, enums and business rules (for example the total equals the sum of line items)
Defensive parsing Never assume the reply is well-formed: wrap parsing in error handling, handle missing or extra fields, empty and refusal responses, and truncation (stop_reason: max_tokens)
Skepticism toward confident output A fluent, confident answer can be wrong: verify against the source, cite the evidence, and route uncertain or high-impact cases to review
Retry with feedback If validation fails, call again with the specific error; stop after a few attempts
  • A schema guarantees shape, not truth: values can still be wrong or invented, so validate meaning and ground answers in the provided documents.
  • Ask the model to quote the source text for key facts so the application can check that the quote exists in the document.
  • Never execute or render model output unsafely (as code, HTML or a database query) without sanitizing it (Module 13).

[Verify live] Structured outputs use output_config.format with a JSON schema, and tools can set strict: true; check the structured outputs page for supported schema features. As of 8 November 2026.

Exam tip

"The model returned plausible but wrong numbers" → validate against the source and add checks; "the JSON sometimes fails to parse" → structured output with a schema plus defensive parsing.

Exam tip

A schema guarantees shape, not truth: validate values against the source and business rules.

4Exam Q&A

S1Summaries from the prompt "Summarize the claim" vary in length and miss key fields. What is the best first improvement?

  • ASwitch to the largest model available and hope the summaries improve
  • BAdd the word "important" in capitals
  • CState audience, exact fields and length, add an example, re-run evals
  • DAsk for a much longer answer so that more fields are included
Show the answer

Answer: C. Clear, specific instructions with a format and examples fix vague output at low cost.

S2Where should the stable role and formatting rules of an assistant go?

  • AIn the system prompt
  • BIn the HTTP headers
  • CIn a random user turn
  • DIn the model name
Show the answer

Answer: A. The system prompt holds stable instructions; the user turn carries the request and data.

S3A prompt mixes instructions with a pasted claim, and the model sometimes treats text inside the claim as instructions. What helps?

  • APut the claim in the system prompt together with all of the instructions
  • BRemove all structure so the model reads the text as one single block
  • CUse a longer claim
  • DTag the data and state that content inside the tags is data, not instructions
Show the answer

Answer: D. Tagging and an explicit data policy reduce confusion between data and instructions.

S4Which technique best shows a model the exact desired output and edge-case handling?

  • AA slower network connection between the app and the API
  • BA higher max_tokens value so the reply has more room
  • CA different API key
  • DA few diverse input and output examples
Show the answer

Answer: D. Few-shot examples demonstrate the exact format and the tricky cases better than long written rules.

S5A parser sometimes fails because the reply contains extra text around the JSON. What is the most reliable fix?

  • ARetry until it parses
  • BAsk politely for valid JSON and say that nothing else may be added
  • CStrip text with a regular expression and hope
  • DUse structured output with a schema and parse defensively
Show the answer

Answer: D. Schema-constrained output removes syntax variation; defensive parsing handles the rest.

S6The model returns valid JSON where the total does not equal the sum of line items. What does this show?

  • AThe model must be retrained before it can add up numbers correctly
  • BSchemas guarantee correct arithmetic
  • CSchemas guarantee shape, not truth: validate meaning too
  • DThe JSON is invalid
Show the answer

Answer: C. Valid structure can hold wrong values; validate business rules.

S7What does skepticism toward confident output mean in practice?

  • ATrust the answer whenever it sounds sure and uses confident wording
  • BRemove all validation
  • CVerify key claims against the source and send uncertain cases to review
  • DAsk the model if it is sure and accept a yes as proof
Show the answer

Answer: C. Fluent confidence is not proof; ground and verify.

S8Which TWO belong to defensive parsing? Select TWO.

  • AValidate types, ranges and required fields after parsing
  • BHandle empty, refused or truncated replies and missing fields without crashing
  • CHide parsing errors from logs
  • DAssume every reply matches the schema
  • EExecute any code the model returns directly
Show the answer

Answer: A, B. Expect malformed or truncated output and validate before use.

S9Which TWO are good prompt iteration practices? Select TWO.

  • AMake prompts longer without checking
  • BKeep prompt versions and results so you can roll back
  • CRewrite everything at once without testing
  • DJudge by one favorite example
  • EChange one thing at a time and measure on a test set
Show the answer

Answer: B, E. Controlled changes with measurement and versioning make improvement reliable.

5Quick Reference Card

Topic Key fact
Clarity Specific task, audience, length, fields, what to do when unsure
Examples 2 to 5 diverse few-shot examples with edge cases
Placement Stable rules in system; request and data in user; tags to separate
Iteration One change at a time, evals, versions, rollback
Sanitization User text is data; escape tag-breaking input; limit length
Structured output output_config.format JSON schema or strict tool schema
Validation Shape ≠ truth: check ranges, business rules, source quotes
Defensive parsing Handle empty, refusal, truncation, missing fields; retry with the error
Skepticism Confident ≠ correct; verify and review high-impact cases
